methodological_questions: Does the teammate with the closest pre-absence initiation profile become the largest gainer in the absent player's primary types?
Can 11 cases and 148 spells support a rank-1 teammate test?
Do similarity, minutes, or usage-matched baselines separate absorption from cascade?
How must gainers and primary types be defined without using the outcome?

historical_evidence.finding: Tested whether a similar-profile teammate separates absorption from cascade when a player sits. Recorded mean similarity ABSORBED +0.863 vs CASCADE +0.848; Spearman(sim, -gap) = -0.19 (wrong-signed). Recorded verdict null, failure type B_powered_null. Sample and power recorded as NOT_RECORDED, and validation status is no_validation_recorded.

Absence validation. Real absences moved the association structure (V1(a) 16/23 above own-null p95, binomial p=2.67e-16; V1(b) CONFIRMED). The simulation prediction of magnitude failed (V2a Spearman +0.288, p=0.077, CI [-0.244, +0.667], FAIL; V2b partial +0.253, p=0.115, FAIL).

Connector absence vs usage-matched others: unmatched D_A 0.2020 vs 0.1021; usage-matched paired dD_A +0.1151, P(conn>ctrl)=81.2%, t=6.35, n=96 pairs. Recorded sample 908 player-seasons. The comparison targets team identity displacement, not teammate-level gain ranking.

On/off identity displacement: shaper vs usage-matched role occupant gave Delta D_A +0.115, t=6.35, shaper larger in 81% of 96 pairs; r(L,D_A)=+0.60. Measures team fingerprint displacement, not which teammate gains.

Holdout play-type rank validation: median rho +0.539; top-3 median hit 100%; median lift +0.4261 PPP; 10.5% of rows had rho<0. Recorded failure mechanism C_artifact, with a doc caveat that top-3 lift partly reflects league-wide high-efficiency play types. Sample 908 rows, 454 games.
Single-game holdout validation (BOS rho 0.200; OKC rho 0.543). Recorded as A_unanswerable: one game with 5-6 play types per team and 4-35 possessions.
Superstar suppression by lineup and forced play type. Recorded as E_unclear, with no placebo or matching; later sequence work treated similar star-chain gaps as artifacts.
Connector presence did not shield stars: dTS +0.05 pp p=0.937; dTO +0.74 pp p=0.00364 (wrong sign); HasConn on-off PPP BOTH_NULL. Lineup lift was a talent confound (p=0.51 after TALENT).

failed_approaches.what_failed: Using pre-absence play-type profile similarity to pick the teammate who absorbs the absent player's usage
failed_approaches.why: Similarity did not separate absorption from cascade and had the wrong sign (Spearman -0.19). Recorded as B_powered_null, but sample and power are NOT_RECORDED, so the null's power is unverified. Similar-profile teammates were almost always findable, which weakens the ranking target.

failed_approaches.what_failed: Simulation-based (LOO) prediction of the magnitude of structural movement under real absence
failed_approaches.why: V2a and V2b failed, with CIs spanning zero at n=23 absence cases. Recorded as untestable, which indicates the absence-case sample was too small to test the magnitude prediction.

failed_approaches.what_failed: Ranking-based play-type validation that looked like a success
failed_approaches.why: Recorded as C_artifact: top-3 lift partly reflected league-wide high-efficiency play types, and 10.5% of rows were misleading. A rank-based success claim can therefore be produced by base-rate structure.

failed_approaches.what_failed: Identifying named star suppressors by lineup and forced play type
failed_approaches.why: No placebo or matching; the mechanism is recorded as unclear (E_unclear), and similar star-chain gaps were later treated as artifacts (PLACEBO_DEPENDENCE).

evidence_establishes: Prior project work on absence and similarity-based redistribution found that similarity-based teammate matching did not separate absorption from cascade (FAM:SF-CHT-052, recorded null).
Rank-based play-type validation in this project was vulnerable to base-rate artifacts (FAM:SF-APPA-063, recorded C_artifact).
Small absence-case samples (n=23 in FAM:SF20; single-game in FAM:SF-APPA-035) left magnitude and rank claims untestable or failed.
evidence_does_not_establish: No retrieved record tests the exact question: whether the rank-1 teammate by pre-absence initiation similarity, minutes, or same-position minutes is the largest gainer in the absent player's primary types.
No retrieved record reports the power or sample for the FAM:SF-CHT-052 null, so its null cannot be treated as adequately powered from the record alone.
No retrieved record uses the 11-case, 148-spell configuration stated for this question.
Connector-absence results (FAM:SF-APPS-088, FAM:SF-PAP-014) concern team-level identity displacement, not teammate-level gain ranking.
own_inferences: With 11 cases and roughly 8-10 eligible teammates each, the chance rank-1 hit rate under a random teammate is about 10-12%, so a useful test needs many more independent cases or a continuous outcome.

The stated question combines three possible profile definitions (closest initiation profile, most minutes, most initiations, same-position minutes), which creates a garden of forking paths unless one is fixed in advance.
Gainers defined by post-absence change in initiations would be outcome-derived, so primary types must be fixed from pre-absence data only.
uncertainties: Whether FAM:SF-CHT-052 used the same absence spells, teammate set, or outcome as this question is not recorded.
The number of absence cases and spells in the historical records is not recorded for most families; only SF20 (n=23) and SF-APPS-088 (n=96 pairs) are quantified.
Whether 2025-26 partial data before the stated cutoffs was used in earlier work is not recorded.
The exact definition of 'largest gainer' and 'primary types' is not given in the task statement.

historical_effect.explanation: The retrieved evidence showed that a similarity-based absorber rule already failed to separate absorption from cascade (FAM:SF-CHT-052, recorded null), that rank-based play-type validation can be an artifact (FAM:SF-APPA-063), and that absence-case samples of this size gave untestable or failed magnitude predictions (FAM:SF20). These records pushed the decision away from proceeding with the confirmatory rank test as posed. The retrieved evidence does not test this exact question, so the decision rests on related prior failures and on the 11-case power constraint, not on a direct prior answer.

blocking_constraints.text: 11 cases give too few independent rank outcomes; a rank-1 hit test has roughly 10-12% chance baseline and cannot reach useful power.
148 spells distributed across 11 cases means many spells per player with few distinct primary types, making per-type gain estimates unstable.
Teammates with high minutes or high usage will often be the largest gainers by construction, so a minutes-based or usage-based baseline may match or beat the similarity rule.
Absences are selected on injury, minutes, or prior bad performance, so the observed gain may reflect regression to the mean rather than the similarity rule.
Defining primary types or gainers from the post-absence change would make the outcome define the test.

prior_work.summary: Related earlier work covered absorption vs cascade by similarity (recorded null, FAM:SF-CHT-052), absence-driven structural movement and magnitude prediction (FAM:SF20, untestable/failed magnitude), rank-based play-type validation (FAM:SF-APPA-063, recorded C_artifact), and connector-absence identity displacement (FAM:SF-APPS-088, FAM:SF-PAP-014, supported). None tests the teammate-level largest-gainer rule with the 11-case design stated here, so the question is only partly answered by analogy.

risks.text: 11 cases and 148 spells are too few for a rank-1 claim at useful power; prior absence validation with 23 cases was already untestable or failed.
Random or minutes-based ranking yields a nontrivial rank-1 hit rate; rank success can be an artifact (FAM:SF-APPA-063).
Absences chosen by injury or poor form make gains look larger without any profile effect.
Minutes, usage, position, and lineup structure jointly drive both similarity and gains; FAM:SF-APPS-087 showed talent confounding of lineup lift.
Gainers and primary types must be fixed from pre-absence data, not from the post-absence outcome.
Play-type classification errors from the play-by-play could mislabel initiations; FAM:SF-CHT-052 cites label or classification error as a limitation.
Without a placebo teammate ranking, star-chain gaps were treated as artifacts (FAM:SF-CHT-009).
Four profile definitions (closest initiation profile, most minutes, most initiations, same-position minutes) create forking paths.
Season-to-season changes in play-type frequencies and roster context across 2022-23 to 2025-26 can shift the baseline (FAM:SF-APPA-063 flags drift risk).
Profile similarity is computed from small per-player samples, reducing reliability (FAM:SF18 flags low measurement reliability).

methodological_questions: Can the teammate with the closest pre-absence initiation profile be identified as the largest gainer in the absent player's primary types?
How many absence spells are needed to test a teammate-ranking claim with 11 cases and 148 spells?
Does regression to the mean or selection on absence length bias gain estimates?
How should gainers and primary types be defined without using the outcome to choose them?

system_prompt:
You are a basketball analytics researcher deciding whether and how a research question should be studied.
You work only from the task statement and the tools listed below. Do not assume facts you have not seen.

The work has two stages, in this order.
Stage 1, retrieval:
1. Read the research objective and the data description.
2. Identify the research concepts and methodological questions the task raises.
3. Retrieve historical evidence by calling retrieve_history.
In stage 1 do not assess the question, predict outcomes or decide. Your only stage-1 reply is the retrieve_history call.
Stage 2, assessment, after the retrieval result is returned:
4. Summarise the relevant historical findings and failed approaches.
5. State what the historical evidence does and does not establish.
6. Assess whether the research question is testable.
7. Identify methodological risks and potential confounders.
8. Make the final research decision.
9. Explain whether and how the historical evidence changed the decision.
The stage-2 output format is given together with the retrieval result.

Evidence rules: keep what a retrieved record states (historical_evidence and failed_approaches, each citing the
identifier of a returned record and its status exactly as recorded) separate from your own inference and from
uncertainty or missing information. Cite only identifiers returned by a tool, and never describe an earlier study that
no tool returned. In some settings retrieval returns no records; then state that no historical evidence was available.

Tools:
- retrieve_history(research_concepts, methodological_questions, query): the prescribed retrieval step. Returns the most relevant consolidated study-family records of earlier research by this project that are available in this setting, with their identifiers; returns an empty list when none are available.
- glossary(): definitions of basketball and project terms used in task statements.
- data_catalog(): the fields available in each per-game data file.
- explore_graph(node_id): the relationships of one graph node (a family or a question, method, dataset, measure, limitation or risk node), with neighbour labels.
- read_family(id): the complete record of one study family (for example 'FAM:SF-APPA-001').

Protocol: every reply is exactly one JSON object and nothing else.
To call a tool: {"action": "tool", "tool": "<name>", "args": {...}}
To finish (stage 2 only): {"action": "final", "output": <object following the stage-2 schema>}
You may call at most 12 tools; then you must finish. Check that every opening brace has a closing brace.

Risk codes (use only these): SAMPLE_SIZE_POWER, EXPOSURE_SPARSITY, MEASURE_RELIABILITY, RTM_SELECTION, OUTCOME_DERIVED_LABEL, LEAKAGE_LOOKAHEAD, MECHANICAL_FLOOR, BASE_RATE, CONFOUNDING, LABEL_ERROR, PLACEBO_DEPENDENCE, MULTIPLE_TESTING, IMPLEMENTATION_BUG, DRIFT_NONSTATIONARITY

The teammate with the closest pre-absence initiation profile (or most minutes / initiations / same-position minutes) is the largest gainer in the absent player's primary types.

Data available on that date:
- NBA 2022-23 regular season and playoffs
- NBA 2023-24 regular season and playoffs
- NBA 2024-25 regular season and playoffs
- NBA 2025-26 regular season (complete from 2026-04-13; partial before)
- NBA 2025-26 playoffs (complete from 2026-06-21; partial before)

- Units available to a study of this question (as recorded): n=148; 148 spells; 11 cases

Your job is to decide, before any analysis is run, whether this question can be answered with this data, what has already been established about it, which methodological and statistical risks threaten a test of it, and either a pre-registration-quality design or a reasoned recommendation not to proceed.
